question: What gave two Chicago hobbyists the time to build the first dial-up bulletin board?
answer: A snowstorm. Snowed in during a heavy Chicago storm in January 1978, Ward Christensen wrote the software and Randy Suess assembled the hardware; CBBS went online on 16 February. It ran on a single phone line, so callers dialled in one at a time and read what the last caller had left.
move: Count the idle weeks behind a breakthrough, not only the talent.
